prompts.A:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: REVIEW-ONLY character sprite art-direction sheet for an original Korean fantasy JRPG; not an in-game screenshot. Input image 1 is the identity/costume reference for male KANG CHUHEUN. Input image 2 is identity/costume reference for female KIM YEONWOO. Redesign these exact two original characters as appealing compact SD overworld pixel-art sprites. Preserve: male short spiky black hair and lively dark eyes; female very long straight black hair with bangs and calm dark eyes; both wear loose black martial arts tunics/trousers, WHITE inner crossover lapel with muted cobalt-blue outer trim and cuffs, small white hollow circular chest emblem, gray cloth waist sash with blue hanging tie, black boots, a SHORT SILVER CHAIN LOOP at hip. Make their black clothes readable with cool blue-gray shading, not pure black masses. No exposed midriff, no armor, no new accessories or weapon replacements.
LAYOUT: landscape canvas, precisely FOUR columns and TWO rows, eight full-body sprites. Entire top row ONLY Chuheun. Entire bottom row ONLY Yeonwoo. Columns left to right: (1) front-facing neutral feet together, (2) right-facing profile neutral, (3) right-facing walking step with one foot forward and opposite arm swing, (4) back-facing neutral. Clear generous transparent gutters. All sprites have consistent stature, head/body size and corresponding foot baseline. Same display height for the two characters. These are samples to judge style, not a battle sheet. Orthographic overworld viewpoint, slight overhead visibility; no perspective foreshortening. TRUE transparent background, no ground, no shadow, no checkerboard, no gradients outside figures, no labels, captions or logos. Render enlarged with nearest-neighbor, hard crisp square pixel clusters, not smooth vector or painted anime. The female hair stays inside the frame and separates from clothing with subtle highlights.
STYLE A: authentic Final Fantasy VI / early 1990s 16-bit SNES field-sprite visual language. About 2.5 heads tall, cute but restrained SD proportions; small plain eyes, broad iconic hair shape. Effective figure resolution about 24 pixels tall (an art-direction target, enlarged for inspection), around 12-16 colors per character, 2 or 3 flat tones per material, bold chunky pixel clusters and simple stepped contours. White collar, blue edging and gray belt must remain distinct. Avoid contemporary high-definition detailing or individual hair strands; don't reduce to the impoverished 14-pixel figure of a tiny prototype. Make an excellent authentic cartridge-era sprite with readable costume.
